newsitem.title: UK: Labour-sees private sector in metro infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: Labour-sees private sector in metro infrastructure.

text.p: The UK Labour shadow transport secretary on Tuesday detailed the party's plans for developing a partnership between the London Underground and the private sector as an alternative to a sell-off.

Andrew Smith, Labour's transport chief, said in a speech at the Industry Forum on transport that a partnership to invest in the cash-strapped London Underground metro system was a half way house between full scale privatisation and retaining the network in the public sector. Smith said the private sector could be used to fund investment in track maintenance, signalling and tunnelling through long-term agreements.

Labour has also suggested establishing "smart card ticketing" for the underground system. This would be an automatic swipe card which could be widened for use in an integrated transport system including the bus network, taxis and suburban trains, he said.
Labour is due to write to London Underground this week to outline its plans to the system.
The policy for the London metro comes amid rumours that the ruling Conservative government will unveil plans to privatise the network as part of its election manifesto.
A UK election is due by May 1997.
